subject: Re: Standard uptime percentage & monthly service credit terms - Cerulean Systems
messages:
From: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cerulean.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Amy Kim <amy.kim@cerulean.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial SLA ask: uptime floor & monthly credit mechanics

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Cerulean is excited about Redwood’s latency profile, but our finance and legal teams have pushed back on the standard SLA credit structure in your template. Two asks from our side:

1) For the first 3 months of the pilot, can we agree to a temporary uptime floor of 99.5% rather than 99.9% to account for our bursty batch traffic during onboarding?
2) We’d like the monthly service credit to scale more granularly for small outages: instead of a single 25% cap, can credits be split into 3 bands (5%, 15%, 25%) based on severity to avoid large one-off impacts on our billing?

I’ve attached the Cerulean redlines for reference (cerulean_sla_redlines.pdf). Can you confirm if Redwood can accept a temporary lower uptime floor for onboarding and provide a tiered monthly credit ladder?

Cheers,
Jordan Patel
Head of Infrastructure
Cerulean Systems

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cerulean.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask: uptime floor & monthly credit mechanics

Jordan—

Appreciate the redlines and the clear asks. Short answer: we can accommodate a temporary onboarding floor and a tiered credit ladder, but we’d like to align on specific guardrails and caps so this scales sensibly if Cerulean goes into production. High-level proposal attached (redwood_sla_draft_v1.pdf). Key points:

- Pilot window: 90 days (start date = first production traffic); uptime floor = 99.5% for pilot only.
- Post-pilot standard = 99.9% uptime.
- Credit ladder for monthly invoice:
  * Severity band A (minor degradation, <0.5% monthly downtime) = 5% credit
  * Band B (0.5%–1.5%) = 15% credit
  * Band C (>1.5%) = 25% credit
- Monthly credit cap at 25% of that month’s invoice (we typically do not exceed 25%).
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance with >48-hour notice is excluded; emergency platform-wide mitigations will be reviewed case-by-case.

Questions for you:
1) Is Cerulean comfortable with a 90-day pilot definition and an automatic reversion to 99.9% after that window?
2) Would you accept the 25% monthly cap if we add SLA-based service credits that are prorated and applied only to impacted product lines?

Looping Ben (pricing) and Laura (legal) to confirm commercial and contract language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cerulean.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask: uptime floor & monthly credit mechanics

Jordan—quick note on pricing implications. If we accept a 99.5% pilot floor (90 days) and allow the tiered credit ladder, two practical items:

- We’ll need a small onboarding fee offset because the pilot increases ops runbook effort and monitoring. I propose a one-time pilot setup fee equal to 10% of the first month’s committed invoice (waived if you convert to annual within 120 days).
- For production, the 25% cap stands. We can add per-product credit anchors so credits only reduce charges tied to impacted product lines (e.g., embeddings vs. generation quotas).

If that’s acceptable I’ll include commercial language in the SOW.

Thanks — Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cerulean.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask: uptime floor & monthly credit mechanics

Jordan / team—

From a legal perspective we can accommodate the pilot floor and tiered credits with the following contract guardrails to limit open liability:

1) Aggregate credit limitation: total credits in a rolling 12-month period will not exceed three times the average monthly spend unless otherwise escalated.
2) Force majeure & maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (≥48h notice) and agreed mitigation plans exempt claims.
3) Incident classification: we will mutually agree on severity definitions in the SOW; credits trigger only after an incident review window (we typically allow 10 business days to reconcile monitoring data).

If Cerulean is comfortable with those three points I’ll prepare redline-friendly contract language.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@cerulean.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amy Kim <amy.kim@cerulean.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask: uptime floor & monthly credit mechanics

Thanks — this is helpful and gets us close. A few quick clarifications from Cerulean finance/legal:

- Pilot setup fee: acceptable if it is credited back (full or partial) on conversion to annual within 120 days. We prefer full credit back on conversion.
- Rolling 12-month credit cap of 3x average monthly spend: Cerulean requests that the cap be measured against the impacted service bill (not company-wide) — that keeps credits proportional to the affected product line.
- Incident review window: 10 business days is fine; can we add a commitment that Redwood will provide incident telemetry exports (redacted) within 3 business days after an incident so we can accelerate reconciliation?

If you can confirm the above items I’ll instruct procurement to move forward with the SOW signature and we can start the pilot the week of Nov 22.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Head of Infrastructure
Cerulean Systems
